metadata.description: The generic engine for AI-driven issue automation across Umbraco products — orchestration, GitHub/CI ops, gated merge, cross-repo dispatch, and the self-learning loop. Product-agnostic: each consumer supplies only a build playbook + a config block. Extracted from the umbraco-mcp-ops prototype.

plugins.name: ops-setup
plugins.description: Interactive onboarding: /umbraco-ops-setup investigates a repo (branching model from git history, CI host, release approach), confirms and fills the gaps via the question tool, then generates the consumer files — .claude/ai-ops.yml, a build-playbook scaffold, any override skills, and the caller workflow(s). Run once per repo after installing the engine.

plugins.name: issue-loop-core
plugins.description: The orchestration engine: work a backlog of ops/ready-for-ai issues to CI-green PRs. Owns the durable /goal loop, rolling cap-3 dispatch, the human-review-response phase, model selection, and stop conditions/backstops. Loads a product's build playbook via a named slot (it does not know how to build any one product). Bundles rework-loop (PR-review-event response). Repo-agnostic; requires github-ops.

plugins.name: github-ops
plugins.description: Shared reference for doing GitHub work two ways — locally with the `gh` CLI + `git`, and on Claude web / in scheduled routines with the GitHub MCP server (`mcp__github__*`). One operation catalog, two reference files; the other loop plugins point here instead of each re-explaining the dual path.

plugins.name: loop-dispatch
plugins.description: Single front door for a repo's automation loops so one routine per repo can handle every loop event instead of one routine per event. Deterministically routes each triggering GitHub event to the matching loop (via route-event.sh); a non-matching event is a quiet no-op. Router only; each loop owns its guardrails. Also bundles new-loop-routine — the single source of truth for standing up a standardised loop routine per repo (config + canonical prompts + UI wiring steps). Repo-agnostic; requires github-ops and the loop skills it routes to.

plugins.name: merge-flow
plugins.description: Guardrail loop that merges PRs labelled `ops/auto-merge` — the maintainer's deliberate go-signal (the human approval, since you can't review-approve your own PR) — but only once they are also CI-green, conflict-free, on the right base, and free of an unresolved 'changes requested'. Replaces error-prone manual merges: it never merges on an unmet gate, and drives each PR to a clean merge (branch deleted) or flags the blocker. Uses /goal so a merge job is provably finished. Repo-agnostic; runs locally or as a scheduled cloud routine.

plugins.name: learning
plugins.description: The self-learning machinery: read-only capture hooks (SubagentStop/SessionEnd) that file proto-learning issues off the critical path, the proto-learning schema, and triage-learnings (dedupe + threshold + route to owning repo / shared-skills PR / loop-improvement issue). Mechanism is generic; the inbox repo and routing table are per-consumer config.

plugins.name: release-flow
plugins.description: Branching, merge, release, and dev-sync workflow skills for any repo — reads the branch model from the consumer's `.claude/ai-ops.yml` (gitflow, main-only, versioned-gitflow, or custom) and resolves base/release_base from config, falling back to branch detection. Branching/merge/release are applied-repo seams: when `branching.release_skill` is set the loop delegates the cut/bump/tag/back-merge mechanics to it and only orchestrates + gates. Bundles release-and-branching, sync-dev (the dev-sync/back-merge/cleanup contract — no engine bash), and auto-release-loop (issue+label-triggered release, two automated gates — green CI + an Opus pre-publish review against a repo-overridable checklist — no approval pause, Claude push notifications).

plugins.name: dotnet-web-runtime
plugins.description: Cloud-environment setup that lets a .NET product run as a Claude web routine: the dotnet-restore internal-NuGet-feed proxy / 401 fix and SessionStart wiring. Needed by any .NET consumer (Forms, Automate); TypeScript products don't need it.
